rows.reference: Hagymasi, Schaefer, Moessner & Luitz, Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 117204 (2021), arXiv:2010.03563 (SU(2) DMRG, best achieved energy; not printed there), as printed in Astrakhantsev et al., Phys. Rev. X 11, 041021 (2021), arXiv:2101.08787, Appendix H Table II, column 'DMRG [38]'

compute.reported_as: Exploiting the SU(2) symmetry of the model [50-53], we keep up to 20000 SU(2) states, (typically equivalent to >~ 80000 U(1) states). [...] For small bond dimensions (chi <~ 2000) we use the two-site version of the DMRG, and switch to the one-site variant to optimize the wave function for larger chi. [...] It turns out that even the calculation of the two-site variance becomes too costly for clusters with more than ~ 100 sites and bond dimensions >~ 8000. In certain cases, we revert to the usage of the two-site DMRG and extrapolate as a function of the truncation error (cf. 108-site cluster). [...] FIG. 5. [...] The corresponding maximal bond dimensions for the 32, 64, 108 and 128-site clusters are 20000, 16000, 16000 and 12000 respectively. [...] Some of the data presented here was produced using the SyTen toolkit, originally created by Claudius Hubig.
compute.source: Hagymasi, Schaefer, Moessner & Luitz, Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 117204 (2021) = arXiv:2010.03563: 'Model and methods'; Fig. 5 caption; Acknowledgments, arXiv:2010.03563 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: bond_dimension = 16000 is the maximal SU(2) bond dimension stated for the 108-site cluster (Fig. 5 caption); the paper's SU(2) states are 'typically equivalent to >~ 80000 U(1) states' at chi = 20000. The 108-site energy was obtained with two-site DMRG and extrapolated in the truncation error (Table I: -0.4935(50) per site extrapolated; the worklist energy corresponds to -0.4851 per site in S-units, i.e. presumably a finite-chi variational value quoted by a later paper rather than the extrapolated value). No CPU hours, core count, wall-clock or machine stated; acknowledgments list only funding and the SyTen toolkit. Worklist had no arXiv id; arXiv 2010.03563 read from the repo cache.

corrections.reported_as: -0.4851 (per site, S.S units, j1 = 1; row 4 x 3^3, column DMRG [38]; footnote 1: 'As the DMRG results, here we show the best actually obtained energy and not the bond-dimension extrapolation.')
corrections.location: arXiv:2101.08787v2 (and v1) Appendix H, Table II, row 4 x 3^3
corrections.version_read: arXiv:2010.03563 v1 and v2 PDFs and LaTeX sources (Table I, all text, Fig. 1 vector data decoded); arXiv:2101.08787 v1 and v2 text (shared cache, VA5 extraction)
corrections.reason: The cited paper does not contain the number: both versions print only the extrapolated 108-site energy, -0.493(4) (v1) and -0.4935(50) (v2), and their Fig. 1 plots only those centres and bars; no text, table or figure gives an achieved finite-bond-dimension energy for 108 sites. The number is printed by Astrakhantsev et al., who quote it from [38] = Hagymasi et al. as 'the best actually obtained energy', and it was uploaded to VarBench by Astrakhantsev (57cdcfe, 2021-07-23, 'DMRG (2010.03563)'). It is consistent with v1's Table I under the paper's own error rule (bar = half the distance from the last point to the extrapolation): -0.493 + 2 x 0.004 = -0.485. Per RULES 8 / DATA.md the row names the producing and the printing paper.

A number quoted from a different paper than the one that produced it is marked secondary (RULES 8, DATA.md 'Provenance and defects'); the VarBench import origin stays in source = varbench@2024-10-22. Apply together with the reference correction, or fold into it if imported rows keep provenance 'imported' by convention.

corrections.location: arXiv:2101.08787v2 Appendix H Table II; VarBench 57cdcfe '| -0.4851 | 0 | ???? |'
corrections.reason: A finite-bond-dimension DMRG energy is deterministic and needs no sigma (RULES 6); no source prints a bar for it, and VarBench's '0' is the uploader's placeholder beside '????' for the variance. A stored 0 claims infinite precision for a number printed to 1e-4 per site and suppresses the no-error-metric marker. One of 8 rows in the table with sigma exactly 0 (the others are exact rows).
